title: Chicken Fried Rice
subtitle: hibachi-style, with garlic butter, egg and soy
imageAlt: Bowl of chicken fried rice with egg, peas and carrots, gold chopsticks
servingsNote: dinner for one big eater + one hungry eater, plus 2 lunches

beforeYouStart.text: Best with cold, day-old rice. No leftovers? Cook the rice, spread it on a sheet pan and chill in the freezer 15 minutes.
Frozen chicken? Thaw it in the fridge overnight.
Chop everything before you turn on the heat — once it starts it moves quickly.

steps.title: Cook the chicken
steps.text: Season the chicken with salt and pepper. Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large skillet or wok over medium-high. Cook 5–7 minutes, stirring now and then, until golden and 74°C (165°F). Move to a plate.

steps.title: Scramble the eggs
steps.text: Melt 1 tbsp butter in the pan, add the eggs and scramble softly, about 1 minute. Add to the chicken.

steps.title: Onion, garlic, veg
steps.text: Add the remaining oil and 1 tbsp butter. Cook the onion 3 minutes, then the garlic and frozen peas & carrots for 2 minutes more.

steps.title: Fry the rice
steps.text: Turn the heat to high. Add the cold rice and last tbsp of butter; break up any clumps and press it flat. Let it sit 1 minute to toast, then stir. Repeat 2–3 times.

steps.title: Sauce and toss
steps.text: Drizzle in the soy and oyster sauce and toss until evenly coloured. Return the chicken and eggs, toss 1 minute, then turn off the heat and stir in the sesame oil. Taste — add a splash more soy if needed.

fixIt.fix: The rice was warm or the pan was crowded. Use cold rice, high heat, and if your pan is small, fry the rice in two batches.
Add soy sauce 1 tsp at a time, plus a pinch of salt. A little more butter brings back the hibachi taste.
Stir in a handful of plain cooked rice or another scrambled egg.
Let the pan get properly hot before the rice goes in, and add a little more oil or butter.

saleTip: No Name frozen peas & carrots and a dozen eggs are cheap staples — buy chicken breast on flyer weeks (around $9–10/kg) and freeze in 600 g bags for this.
swap: Swap the chicken for shrimp, or use leftover rotisserie chicken (add it at the end).
leftovers: Fridge 3–4 days — great for lunch. Microwave with a damp paper towel on top until steaming (74°C / 165°F). Freezes well for 2 months.
source: Classic restaurant fried-rice method (cold rice, high heat, soy + oyster sauce); safe temp per Health Canada.
prepAhead: Cook the rice a day ahead — cold rice makes the best fried rice.
Dice the chicken and onion and mince the garlic the night before.
reheat: Microwave with a damp paper towel on top, stirring halfway, until steaming (74°C / 165°F), or toss in a hot skillet with a little butter.
